resources.string: Your key is backed up, and your account has a passphrase you can recover.
Losing this phone would lose your identity. Until you back it up, it can\'t approve anything.
Make recovery codes and keep them apart from your accounts and passkeys.
Your account\'s passphrase, recovery and sign-ins are kept by your home node. Join a node to set them up.
Tap to unlock with your screen lock.
Your identity\'s key isn\'t backed up yet. Until you\'ve saved it and checked the copy, it can\'t change your passphrase, link accounts or renew this phone\'s key.
Changes to your account at the node need it, even with your key. The screen lock protects this phone; the passphrase protects your account.
A passphrase protects your account at the node even if your key leaks.
At least 8 characters, at least 5 of them different
This account already has a passphrase. Enter it to change it.
Choose a passphrase you will remember. The node asks for it for changes to your account, even when they are made with your key.
Next you get recovery codes: each resets the passphrase once if you forget it.
Passphrase set, but recovery codes couldn\'t be made: %1$s Make them under Recovery.
Enter your current passphrase, then the new one.
Changes to your account will then need only your key. Enter your passphrase to remove it.
Each resets a forgotten passphrase once.
Linked accounts (%1$d) and passkeys (%2$d) can reset it too.
No way to reset a forgotten passphrase
If you forget your passphrase, it can\'t be reset. Make recovery codes now.
Recovery codes reset a forgotten passphrase, once each.
New codes replace the earlier ones, which stop working. Enter your passphrase to make them.
This account has no passphrase, so it has no recovery codes.
Reset it without the old one. Your identity\'s key alone can\'t do it: choose one of the ways you set up.
No recovery code, linked account or passkey is set up for this account, so the passphrase can\'t be reset.
The node lists no account providers right now.
Use a passkey, on the web
A passkey works only on your node\'s website. This opens your node\'s portal: choose \"Forgot passphrase?\" there.
Enter one of your recovery codes. It works only once.
That code is wrong or has been used.
Choose a new passphrase. Finish now: the reset is good only for a few minutes, and closing this loses it.
The reset took too long. Start again.
That account couldn\'t reset the passphrase. It may not be linked to this identity.
Your new passphrase is set. Use it from now on.
Finish in the browser. When it\'s done, you come back here.
The account provider or the node refused (%1$s).
No linked accounts. A linked account signs in to your node\'s web portal as you, and can reset a forgotten passphrase.
This node doesn\'t list linked accounts.
It will no longer sign in as you, or reset your passphrase.
Your account has a passphrase. Unlinking needs it.
Your %1$s account will no longer sign in as you at %2$s
Choose where your account is. You sign in there, in the browser, and come back here.
This node doesn\'t sign in with any account provider.
Link your %1$s account to your identity at %2$s?
Your account has a passphrase. Linking needs it.
Your %1$s account will sign in as you at %2$s
Your %1$s account now signs in to your node\'s web portal as you, and can reset a forgotten passphrase.
This account is already linked to another identity. Unlink it there first.
The sign-in expired. Choose the account again to sign in once more.
Passkeys are added in your node\'s web portal and approved here, with \"Approve a new device\" in Devices. Remove them in Devices.
Passphrase reset with a recovery code
Passphrase reset with a linked account
Web portal signed in with Boson Identity
Admin dashboard signed in with Boson Identity
Web page signed in with Boson Identity
Show and back up my key
Save your identity\'s key as a file, a QR code or text.
Give this phone a new key of its own, and remove the old one from the node.
This phone gets a new key of its own, and the old one is removed from the node. Your identity and its key don\'t change. Do this if you think this phone\'s key may have been exposed.
Your account has a passphrase. Renewing this phone\'s key needs it.
This phone will use a new key at %1$s
This phone\'s new key will be stored encrypted
The node took the new key, but this phone couldn\'t store it.
If you cancel, this phone will have to join the node again.
This phone has a new key
The old key no longer works at the node.
The old key couldn\'t be removed from the node. Remove it in Devices: it is the other \"Boson Identity\" on this phone\'s name.
Your identity\'s key is encrypted on this phone. Every time it is used, the phone asks for your fingerprint or screen lock.
On. A new phone with your synced passkey can restore this identity.
Off. An extra copy of your key that a passkey in your password manager can open on a new phone.
Not available on this phone: it needs Google Play services and a Google account to back up to.
Check your own backup of the key first. The passkey backup is an extra copy, never the only one.

A copy of your identity\'s key is stored with your Google account, locked by a new passkey. Anyone who controls your Google account and can unlock it with your screen lock on another phone could restore this identity. Keep your own backup too.
This passkey provider can\'t protect a backup. Try Google Password Manager.
A copy of your key will be locked by the new passkey
Check that it was you: a device added or a sign-in you didn\'t make means someone else has access.
Made an administrator of this node by its owner
Made an administrator of this node by %1$s
